facts.text: The study compared equiatomic CrFeTaVW with CrFeTiVW, in which Ta was replaced by Ti.
Conventional molecular dynamics was compared with hybrid MD/Monte Carlo simulations that allowed unlike-atom swaps.
Elemental powder mixtures were mechanically alloyed by planetary ball milling at 350 rpm for 2 h using WC media and a 10:1 ball-to-powder ratio.
The principal spark-plasma-sintering treatment was conducted at 1543 K and 70 MPa for 5 min.
Laser-flash thermal diffusivity was measured from 300 to 1000 K under 0.05 bar helium.
The simulations used periodic NPT cells at 1 atm for 6×10^6 time steps, with an attempted unlike-atom swap every 10 MD steps in the hybrid method.
Hybrid atom swaps produced lower-potential-energy chemical configurations than conventional MD for both alloys.
CrFeTiVW showed stronger simulated W-related segregation and enhanced W–W association than CrFeTaVW, with the segregation tendency peaking near 1200 K.
Strongly negative Fe–Ta mixing enthalpy and atomic-size mismatch were identified as drivers of Fe2Ta C14 Laves-phase formation during consolidation.
After sintering, CrFeTaVW contained a bcc matrix plus Fe2Ta C14 Laves phase, whereas CrFeTiVW contained two bcc-derived phases.

Replacing Ta with Ti did not materially change thermal diffusivity; both alloys showed a slight increase in diffusivity with increasing temperature and remained substantially less diffusive than W and CuCrZr.
The measured thermal diffusivity of both consolidated alloys was approximately 3.5–7 mm²/s over 300–1000 K.
